# Xbox HDD test fixtures

Small xemu-style disk images for `tests/xbox_tests.rs`. The data is synthetic: made-up title ids and
generated bytes, no game content.

They are built by **independent** implementations, so the Rust qcow2/FATX reader is checked against
code it shares nothing with:

| piece | built / read by |
|---|---|
| FATX formatting and every file written | libfatx, via `pyfatx` (GPL-2.0-or-later) |
| qcow2 files (v3, v2, zlib-compressed, 4 KiB clusters) | `qemu-img convert` (real QEMU output; each passes `qemu-img check`) |
| `manifest.json` (expected files, sizes, md5s) | re-reading the finished volume through libfatx, then asserted against what the generator meant to write |

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `hdd-v3.qcow2` | QEMU default: v3, 64 KiB clusters |
| `hdd-v2.qcow2` | legacy v2 (`compat=0.10`) |
| `hdd-compressed.qcow2` | zlib-compressed clusters (`-c`) |
| `hdd-4k.qcow2` | 4 KiB clusters, so many L2 tables |
| `small-fat16.qcow2` | a 32 MiB FAT16 partition at offset `0x100000` (E: is always FAT32) |

Partition E sits where a retail disk puts it (`0xABE80000`, `0x1312D6000` long), 16 KiB clusters.

What the content covers: multi-cluster files, an exactly-one-cluster file, an empty file, deep nesting,
a directory spanning two clusters (300 entries), deleted entries on both sides of a live one, a stray
file and a non-title folder in `UDATA`, a title folder with no files, and a `TDATA` folder.

Two reference-tool quirks the generator works around (see the comments in `gen_fixtures.py`):

* pyfatx's `listdir()` stops at the first deleted entry (libfatx itself skips and continues).
* libfatx cannot grow a directory past one cluster, and refuses 42-character names (the on-disk field
  holds 42). The grown directory is added by raw writes; the 42-byte name is covered by a synthetic
  volume in the Rust tests instead.

Regenerate (needs `pip install pyfatx` and `qemu-img`):

```
python3 gen_fixtures.py
```

The qcow2 bytes differ with the QEMU version; the tests compare against `manifest.json`, which is
regenerated with them.
